If a Christian dies
with a sin they have not yet had time to confess,
will they lose their right to enter the Kingdom of Heaven?  

Some people say,
“Once you believe, you are always saved.”
But Jesus said:
“Except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.”
Luke 13:3 KJV.
The problem is,
many people misunderstand repentance.
Do you think repentance is simply crying
and saying, “I’m sorry”?
No.
True repentance is not just temporary regret.
It is a change of mind
that leads to a change of direction.
Look at David and the people of Nineveh.
They were not only sorrowful over sin;
they were willing to turn from it.
That is the change true repentance should produce.
Imagine this:
A guilty person receives mercy from a judge.
That is grace.
But if he uses that mercy as a reason to keep doing wrong,
does he truly understand grace?
In John 8, Jesus said:
“Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin.”
Then He said:
“If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.”
Forgiveness is not permission to keep sinning.
True grace does not teach us
to become comfortable living in sin.
So the real question is not only:
“Did I have time to confess every single sin before I died?”
The deeper question is:
Do I truly trust Christ?
Am I willing to repent?
Or am I knowingly continuing in sin
while using grace as an excuse?
Of course,
we cannot overcome sin simply by our own strength.
That is why Jesus promised the Holy Spirit.
John 16:13 says:
“When he, the Spirit of truth, is come,
he will guide you into all truth.” KJV.
You do not have to struggle alone.
Depend on the Lord
and walk with the Holy Spirit in truth.
If this message reminded you,
write Amen in the comments.
Share it with someone
who may misunderstand grace and repentance.
